title: UE 5 — Fraud Considerations
subtitle: Section A: 11 fraud considerations with auto-classification
issai_reference: ISSAI 2240 / ISA 240 — The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud in an Audit of FS
psrec_note: ISSAI 2240 anchors: Q3 (management override) is a PRESUMED FRAUD RISK requiring JE testing regardless of answer. Revenue-related questions are presumed fraud risks. Any 'Yes' answer triggers a row on the Risks Identified register.

sections.title: Fraud Risk Considerations
sections.guidance: Yellow = auditor input. Orange = risk identified. Green = clear. Apply PSREC for the Record of Work Done on every question.

questions.text: Has management identified any fraud or suspected fraud during the period, and what was the response?
questions.guidance: A Yes answer triggers immediate escalation requirements under ISSAI 2240.
questions.risk_description: Fraud identified or suspected by management — immediate escalation required under ISSAI 2240.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Identified or suspected fraud is a fundamental indicator of risk affecting the integrity of financial reporting and the control environment.

questions.text: Are employees or non-management personnel aware of any instances where management has not responded appropriately to identified misstatements?
questions.risk_description: Misstatements not addressed by management — tone-at-the-top and override risk.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Failure to respond appropriately to known misstatements indicates a weak control environment and potential management override.

questions.text: Are there incentives or pressures on management that could lead to fraudulent financial reporting?
questions.guidance: ISSAI 2240 ¶31: management override of controls is a PRESUMED FRAUD RISK — JE testing is mandatory regardless of this answer.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Identified fraud incentives or pressures on management increase the likelihood of intentional misstatement.

questions.text: Have significant or unusual transactions occurred during the year (e.g., large year-end transactions, related-party transactions, related-party balances)?
questions.risk_description: Significant or unusual transactions identified — heightened audit risk in procurement, accruals, capex.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Unusual or complex transactions increase the risk of misstatement, particularly where they are non-recurring or involve related parties.

questions.text: Are there indications of unusual or material expenses (such as travel, subsistence, entertainment, allowances)?
questions.risk_description: Unusual or material expenses identified — potential misappropriation risk.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Unusual or material discretionary expenses may indicate misappropriation, ghost employees or misclassification.

questions.text: Has management displayed behaviours that undermine auditor confidence (e.g., delays in providing information, restrictions on access)?
questions.risk_description: Management behaviour undermines auditor confidence — potential scope limitation.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Behaviour that obstructs the audit may indicate concealment of misstatement and constitutes a pervasive risk to the engagement.

questions.text: Do performance measures, KPIs, or external pressures exist that may create incentives for fraudulent financial reporting?
questions.risk_description: Performance pressure creates incentive for fraudulent financial reporting (especially revenue, provisions, accruals).
questions.inherent_risk_factor: External or internal performance pressure incentivises bias in estimates, revenue recognition and accrual timing.

questions.text: Has management assessed the risk of fraud in the entity and implemented procedures to mitigate it?
questions.risk_description: Management has not performed a fraud risk assessment — weak fraud governance.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: The absence of a management-led fraud risk assessment indicates an immature fraud governance environment, increasing inherent fraud risk.

questions.text: Has the presumed risk of fraud in revenue recognition been considered, and if rebutted, has it been documented?
questions.guidance: ISSAI 2240 ¶26: revenue recognition is a PRESUMED FRAUD RISK. Rebuttal must be documented.
questions.risk_description: Revenue recognition fraud risk not considered or rebuttal not documented — ISSAI 2240 non-compliance.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Revenue is a presumed fraud risk; failure to document consideration or rebuttal exposes the audit to ISSAI 2240 compliance risk and undocumented risk acceptance.

questions.text: Have inquiries been made of internal audit (where the function exists) regarding fraud-related work performed?
questions.risk_description: Internal audit not consulted on fraud — corroborative evidence missing.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Failure to consult internal audit on fraud-related work weakens the auditor's risk assessment process under ISSAI 2240.

questions.text: Has the engagement team held a discussion (fraud brainstorming) on susceptibility of the FS to material misstatement due to fraud?
questions.risk_description: No engagement team fraud brainstorming — ISSAI 2240 ¶15 non-compliance.
questions.inherent_risk_factor: Failure to conduct a documented fraud brainstorming session at planning indicates the team has not formally considered susceptibility to fraud — a pervasive engagement-level weakness.
